# google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model

Deploys an existing Vertex AI Model to an existing Endpoint.


To get more information about EndpointDeployedModel, see:

* [API documentation](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/reference/rest/v1/projects.locations.endpoints/deployModel)
* How-to Guides
    * [Vertex AI online prediction](https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/docs/predictions/overview)

## Example Usage - Vertex Ai Endpoint Deployed Model Basic


```hcl
resource "google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model" "deployment" {
  endpoint = google_vertex_ai_endpoint.endpoint.id
  region   = "us-central1"
  model    = "projects/vertex-ai/locations/us-central1/models/model-name"

  dedicated_resources {
    min_replica_count = 1

    machine_spec {
      machine_type = "n1-standard-4"
    }
  }
}

resource "google_vertex_ai_endpoint" "endpoint" {
  display_name = "endpoint-endpoint-name"
  location     = "us-central1"
  region       = "us-central1"
}
```

## Argument Reference

The following arguments are supported:


* `model` -
  (Required)
  The full resource name of the Model to deploy.

* `endpoint` -
  (Required)
  The existing Vertex AI Endpoint to deploy the model to.

* `region` -
  (Required)
  The region of the Endpoint.


* `display_name` -
  (Optional)
  The display name of the deployed model.

* `dedicated_resources` -
  (Optional)
  Dedicated resources for serving the model.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_dedicated_resources).

* `automatic_resources` -
  (Optional)
  Automatic resources for serving the model.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_automatic_resources).

* `traffic_split` -
  (Optional)
  A JSON map from deployed model IDs to traffic percentages.

* `deletion_policy` - (Optional) Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the resource. Defaults to DELETE.
	When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the resource,
	the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
	When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
	management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
	When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.

* `machine_spec` -
  (Required)
  A nested object resource.
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_dedicated_resources_machine_spec).

* `min_replica_count` -
  (Required)

* `max_replica_count` -
  (Optional)

* `autoscaling_metric_specs` -
  (Optional)
  Structure is [documented below](#nested_dedicated_resources_autoscaling_metric_specs).


<a name="nested_dedicated_resources_machine_spec"></a>The `machine_spec` block supports:

* `machine_type` -
  (Optional)

* `accelerator_type` -

## Attributes Reference

In addition to the arguments listed above, the following computed attributes are exported:

* `id` - an identifier for the resource with format `{{endpoint}}/deployedModels/{{deployed_model_id}}`

* `deployed_model_id` -
  The numeric ID of the deployed model. If omitted, Vertex AI assigns one.


## Timeouts

This resource provides the following
[Timeouts](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/plugin/sdkv2/resources/retries-and-customizable-timeouts) configuration options:

- `create` - Default is 60 minutes.
- `update` - Default is 0 minutes.
- `delete` - Default is 30 minutes.

## Import


EndpointDeployedModel can be imported using any of these accepted formats:

* `projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/endpoints/{{endpoint}}/deployedModels/{{deployed_model_id}}`
* `{{project}}/{{region}}/{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}`
* `{{region}}/{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}`
* `{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}`

In Terraform v1.12.0 and later, use an [`identity` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/block/import#identity) to import EndpointDeployedModel using identity values. For example:

```tf
import {
  identity = {
    endpoint = "<-required value->"
    region = "<-required value->"
    deployedModelId = "<-optional value->"
  }
  to = google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default
}
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import EndpointDeployedModel using one of the formats above. For example:

```tf
import {
  id = "projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/endpoints/{{endpoint}}/deployedModels/{{deployed_model_id}}"
  to = google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default
}
```

When using the [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import), EndpointDeployedModel can be imported using one of the formats above. For example:

```
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default projects/{{project}}/locations/{{region}}/endpoints/{{endpoint}}/deployedModels/{{deployed_model_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default {{project}}/{{region}}/{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default {{region}}/{{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}
$ terraform import google_vertex_ai_endpoint_deployed_model.default {{endpoint}}/{{deployed_model_id}}
```
